title: URL Shortener
brief: Build a URL shortener. POST /shorten takes a long URL and returns a short code; GET /<code> redirects to the long URL. Same product, two traffic shapes.

variants.twist: A celebrity posts a short link: traffic ×5 for 60 s. Apply with spike(5, 60).
The partner doubles their import rate: 20k rps at the same mix. Apply with set_traffic(rps=20000).

hints: At the variant's traffic, which block hits its limit first? Run it and check the saturation list.
Reads and writes scale differently. Caches and read replicas only take reads off the database.
Read-heavy: a cache in front of the database, and enough service replicas for 10k rps. Write-heavy: a store that spreads writes over nodes (NoSQL / KV) instead of one SQL primary.
_notes: Service 1k rps/replica at 20 ms; in the sim p99 is about 10x a block's own queueing latency, so the service needs rho ~0.6 (16 replicas, $1.60) for p99 < 250 ms (sim: 181 ms; 14 replicas gives 262 ms). SQL primary 5k rps ($0.50). Read-heavy: 9.9k reads overload one DB; a cache (hit 0.9 x read share 0.99 with invalidate) leaves ~1.1k reads + 100 writes. ~$2.25/hr. Write-heavy: 6k writes/s > one primary's 5k; cache and replicas don't help. KV 3 x 10k = 30k ops/s ($0.90): ~$2.50/hr. Over-provisioning (30 service replicas + 5 read replicas) breaks the cost limit. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
